Start with a disposable VPS.

This is an early alpha. Read the completed tests and remaining gates before relying on it.

I’m the administrator.

Deploy, connect and manage through Rookstride.

01

Get ready

Use Android 8 or later and a fresh Ubuntu 24.04 VPS (two distinct fresh nodes for the two-server route) with a public IPv4 address. The installer supports x86_64 and aarch64; the live server cycles used x86_64. Have root or passwordless sudo SSH access.

Allow inbound UDP 500 and 4500 for IKEv2, plus your SSH port. Keep the phone online and the VPS able to download Ubuntu packages and AdGuard Home. Bundled installation code does not make this an Internet-free installation.

02

Install the signed app

Download and verify the APK, then open it on Android. Your download app may ask for permission to install this APK. Only use the project’s signed release and retain the matching source/checksum references.

You can explore the labeled offline demo and built-in guide before adding a real server.

03

Add and trust your gateway

Choose Add gateway. Enter its address, SSH port, administrator name, and password or private key. For examples, use vpn.example.net; enter your own server in the app.

Inspect the gateway. Compare the presented SSH host-key fingerprint with your provider console or another trusted route before trusting it. Rookstride pins that key and refuses a changed key.

Optional saved credentials use Android Keystore encryption. Leaving “remember” off keeps them in app memory until the process ends.

04

Install the gateway

On a fresh server, choose Install gateway on fresh VPS. Create the first VPN login with a unique password and decide whether to enable estimated usage history.

The app transfers its installer over SSH and starts a detached job on the VPS. If the phone disconnects, reconnect to check status: the server job continues. A VPS reboot during installation can interrupt it and leave partial state.

The fresh-install guard refuses an existing VPN/DNS setup. Inspect a failed job before rebuilding; do not force the installer over a working gateway.

05

Connect on this phone

Open People, select a VPN login, and choose Use on this phone. Enter its VPN password, approve Android’s VPN and background-operation prompts, then connect from the gateway screen.

Your VPN login is separate from root/SSH and the AdGuard dashboard login. Only one Android VPN can be active at a time.

06

Check the actual route

On the connected device, check that websites open, that the exit IPv4 matches your chosen VPS, that an advertising test domain is blocked, and that no unexpected public IPv6 appears. Repeat over both Wi-Fi and mobile data.

The profile uses MTU 1280 and full IPv4/IPv6 selectors. IPv6 Internet egress is intentionally unavailable. Rookstride’s own SSH/certificate-fetch traffic is exempt from its tunnel; use another browser/app for route checks.

For blocking while disconnected, configure Android’s Always-on VPN / Block connections without VPN settings and test their behavior on your phone.

TWO-SERVER RECIPE

Bring two nodes.

Choose Add a two-server gateway, enter separate entry and exit SSH details, and independently verify both identities. The app prepares the exit first, joins the bridge, checks the route, and then opens client forwarding. Your phone uses IKEv2; the bridge uses AmneziaWG 3.1. DNS filtering lives at the exit.

Follow eight checkpoints, or read the guide and stories while the installation service continues. The progress shortcut and notification return to the current step. Single-server installation has five checkpoints; enrollment has four. Time ranges are broad planning estimates, with elapsed time shown separately.

Reviewed reset and role-swap controls support a fresh reinstall. Reset removes recognized owned gateway data; a complete operating-system rebuild belongs in the provider console. Read the pair setup and recovery guide before deployment.

SHARED ACCESS

I’ve been invited.

You do not need the administrator’s SSH access or Rookstride. Get the official strongSwan Android client.

  1. Receive your .sswan profile and VPN password separately from the administrator, over a trusted channel.
  2. Open or import the profile in strongSwan. It contains the server certificate and your login, without a VPN password or root access.
  3. Enter your VPN password, approve the Android VPN prompt, and connect.
  4. Check websites, exit IPv4, DNS filtering and IPv6 on the actual phone. Ask for a fresh profile after a server reset: a new installation has new certificates.
One login, several devices?

That is supported, with combined usage totals. Ask for a separate device login for individual revocation and clearer estimates. The login is not tied to physical hardware.

A QUIETER ROUTE

Choose your DNS filter.

In Rookstride, open Gateways → AdGuard controls. Increase one level at a time and check your usual sites afterward.

01

Standard

AdGuard DNS filter

A starting point for common ads and trackers.
02

Strong

HaGeZi Pro

Broader filtering. Check for broken site features.
03

Strict

HaGeZi Pro++

Most aggressive preset. More false positives are possible.

For custom lists and allow rules, connect to the VPN and open http://10.254.0.1:3000, unless your DNS address was changed. It is a private dashboard inside the encrypted tunnel, with a separate login in /root/single-vps-vpn/adguard-login.txt on the server.

In AdGuard, use Filters → DNS blocklists for lists and Filters → Custom filtering rules for individual rules. If a site breaks, return to Standard or allow a required domain.

DNS filters have a specific job.

They block separate ad/tracker domains. They cannot reliably remove YouTube in-video ads, fix a datacenter IP’s reputation, or stop location signals from accounts, GPS and cookies. Apps with their own encrypted DNS may bypass filtering.

READ THE SIGNS

If something fails.

The VPN says “peer not responding.”+

Check the entered server address and the VPS’s availability. Verify the provider firewall and server rules permit UDP 500/4500. Try both Wi-Fi and mobile data. Reaching an HTTPS website on the server only proves TCP reachability; it does not prove IKEv2 UDP reaches it. Compare client and server logs.

The VPN says “authentication failed.”+

Check the VPN login and password, not the root/SSH credentials. Confirm the account is active and the profile has the current server certificate. After resetting/reinstalling, export a new profile.

It connects, but websites do not load.+

Separate routing from DNS: compare a connected browser’s exit IPv4 and check name resolution. Confirm the private AdGuard/Unbound services are healthy. Return to Standard filtering or review the AdGuard query log for a false positive. Use the project operations guide for server checks.

A website says I am in another country.+

Compare the detected IP with the VPS’s public IPv4 first. Geolocation databases may classify the VPS differently from its hosting label. Sites can also use login history, cookies, GPS or browser signals. A VPN does not change those signals or guarantee access to sites that reject datacenter addresses.

The SSH fingerprint has changed.+

Stop and verify through your provider console. A server rebuild can change a key, but a changed key is also a reason to investigate. Do not accept it only to get past the warning.

More detail: app operations · gateway operations.

A NEW BEGINNING

Reset with a clear plan.

Reset gateway data reviews the recognized files and services first. Its review token lasts five minutes. Applying it requires typing DELETE VPN.

It permanently removes gateway accounts, certificates, AdGuard data, managed firewall rules and traffic history. Connected users lose access. Ubuntu, SSH, unrelated files and package binaries remain. A complete operating-system wipe is a provider control-panel operation.

Unknown configurations, extra VPN connections, symlinked managed paths, changed plans and active installation jobs are refused. The server must be reachable. After reinstalling, export fresh profiles for every user.

For a compatible existing gateway, Manage an existing gateway explicitly enrolls the helper. Back up first; arbitrary strongSwan setups are not automatically compatible.
